🇺🇸 US midterms: Democrats win both houses of Congress. What it means for Mzansi 🇿🇦

On 3 November Americans voted for all 435 seats in the House, about a third of the Senate and 36 governors. Results so far give Democrats control of both the House and the Senate (some races are still being counted). The House is elected every 2 years, senators every 6 (a third at a time) and the president every 4, so Donald Trump stays president until January 2029, but now faces a Congress that can block his laws and budgets. The new Congress starts on 3 January 2027.

Can it save South Africa's AGOA access? Not quickly. A day before the vote, Trump told Congress that South Africa and Rwanda will lose their AGOA duty-free access from 1 January 2027. That's a power the President holds; reversing it would most likely need a new law, which he can veto. But Congress decides AGOA's renewal, and countries can be reinstated (Gabon was, in May 2026). South Africa has 60 days to appeal.

What's at stake: about $1.7 billion of SA exports used AGOA in 2025, roughly 10% of what we sell to the US. Citrus, macadamias and some food exports face higher tariffs; most minerals and metals don't rely on AGOA.

Will the new Congress push Washington to change course? 👇
